Education, Lecture

[Online] Visual archives as a means to process trauma: Azza El-Hassan

30 September, 2026
– 30 September, 2026
5-6pm BST
Online (Zoom or Youtube)
BOOK

Plain English

Audio Version

(Listening Time: 4 minutes)

Event: Visual archives as a means to process trauma: Azza El-Hassan

The fourth online lecture in the ‘Sharing Strategies: Caring for moving image in the margins’ programme will see Azza El-Hassan reflect on her work with archival material documenting colonial violence and plunder and the reclamatory potential that this material holds when it is not only preserved, but put to use. 

El-Hassan is a filmmaker and researcher and in 2019, founded The Void Project, a multimedia production space that investigates artistically the visual effect of colonial plunder on the formation of a modern Palestinian narrative. Her book, ‘The Afterlife of Palestinian Images’, uniquely addresses how plundered cultures relate to the actual remains of their archives. 

In this lecture, El-Hassan will explore the visual remains of plunder – photos, films and media equipment that have survived a violent event and emerged damaged by the violence. She will reflect on her seven-year journey through ‘The Void Project’ searching for encounters with visual remains of plunder and address why it remains important to not only find and document these objects but to put them into use.

El-Hassan will discuss how an interaction with visual remains of plunder for a person who has, just like these objects, been subjected to colonial violence can prove to be riddled with ethical and confrontational findings. Despite these challenges, she will argue that these encounters are necessary for both the object and subject of the encounter in order to process violence and produce a new, modern visual experience. 

This is the fourth in a series of five online lectures taking place as part of ‘Sharing Strategies: Caring for moving image in the margins.’ This programme provides a platform for conservators, archivists, researchers and artist-filmmakers to share their community-led practices, and the ways knowledge is produced collectively, often in informal, under-resourced or under-recognised settings. More details and recordings of past lectures can be found here.

 

What to expect:

  • The event will take place online, on Zoom and Youtube
  • It will be one hour long in total, including time for audience questions
  • The event will be free
  • The Zoom has limited capacity and is now fully booked.
  • You will also be able watch live via our Youtube channel. The stream will be available on this link and booking is not required to watch via Youtube
  • Live captions will be available on both platforms
  • The event will be recorded and made available to watch back later

About the contributor

Azza El-Hassan is a filmmaker and a Professor of Media practices at the Doha Institute for Graduate Studies. She is known for The Unbearable Presence of Asmahan (2014), Kings & Extras (2004), and News Time (2001).She is the winner of various international film awards and the recipient of the 2025, BAFTSS Outstanding Achievement Award. In 2019, she founded The Void Project, a multimedia production space, that investigates artistically the visual effect of colonial plunder on the formation of a modern Palestinian narrative. Her book, The Afterlife of Palestinian Images, uniquely addresses how plundered cultures relate to the actual remains of their archives.

 

Delivered with the support of the BFI Screen Heritage Fund, awarding National Lottery funding.
